messages:

Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Exploring committed spend options for 2027

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to get more concrete around a committed spend structure for calendar 2027. High level: we expect bursty usage during clinical reporting cycles (Q1 & Q3) and relatively low baseline otherwise. Our procurement prefers a prepaid model (prepay wallet) with a usage-based drawdown rather than a fixed monthly invoice. Key asks:

- Can Redwood support an annual prepay that we can draw from as tokens are consumed?
- We need a predictable term discount that improves with a multi-year cadence (1yr vs 3yr).
- Any ability to smooth the effective burn for months with spikes (e.g., ramp credits, monthly top-ups triggered by threshold)?

Attached is our standard procurement template — we can share numbers if the structure is workable.

Liam
CTO, Veridian Health
liam.oconnor@veridianhealth.com

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay model — high-level options and examples

Hi Liam —

Appreciate the clear asks. Redwood supports a wallet-style prepay with a usage-based drawdown and several levers to manage bursty workloads. At a high level we can offer:

1) Annual prepay wallet: you pre-fund credits (USD value) that decrement as tokens are consumed. Credits can be denominated and consumed in USD/token-equivalent.
2) Multi-year term discounts: standard tiers for 1yr / 2yr / 3yr (we can put numbers in a term sheet) — discounts apply to the full committed annual spend, not incremental usage.
3) Ramp smoothing options: two approaches — (a) Managed monthly smoothing: we amortize the prepaid balance over 12 months for internal reporting while still allowing full drawdown on spikes; (b) Threshold top-ups: automated monthly top-ups when on-hand credits fall below X% to avoid interruptions.

I'll attach a worked example (spreadsheet) showing a 3-year commit with annual prepay, a quarterly spike profile, and two smoothing options. Rafael from pricing is CC'd — he can confirm discount bands and the recommended billing/legal language for the MOA.

Next steps: if you can share an expected annual spend range (ballpark) and the expected spike multiple (e.g., 3x in Q1/Q3) we will put together a formal term-sheet and an example wallet burn schedule.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Prepay model — discount bands and billing implications

Vanessa / Liam —

Quick pricing note from our side: for a usage-drawdown prepay we recommend structuring discounts as follows (draft guidance):

- 1yr commit: 10% off list for the committed annual USD value when prepaid
- 2yr commit: 15% off list
- 3yr commit: 20% off list

Important billing/legal points:
- Prepaid funds are non-refundable but transferable across product routes under the same legal entity.
- We offer an optional quarterly reconciliation true-up to align committed volume to actual usage; overages billed at list or at a pre-agreed overage rate.
- For smoothing: we can provide a monthly amortization statement (internal only) while the actual wallet reduces on consumption. That gives finance-friendly monthly effective cost figures without constraining availability.

I ran a couple of quick scenarios in the attached spreadsheet and highlighted a 3-year path that yields ~18% blended discount if Veridian commits to a 2.5x peak multiple.

Rafael

Subject: Re: Prepay model — answers + worked example

Sarah / Liam —

Answers inline and a clear worked example below (pulled from the attached spreadsheet):

1) Monthly burn options:
- Consumption-driven: wallet decrements only when tokens are used. Your invoice shows consumption and the remaining prepaid balance.
- Fixed internal amortization: we provide an optional monthly amortized ledger for your FP&A that spreads the prepaid spend (e.g., $360k / 12 = $30k/month) for budget reporting. This does not affect availability — you can still consume the full balance in high months.

2) Underutilization policy:
- Standard: prepaid funds are non-refundable.
- Credit carryforward: for multi-year commitments we offer a one-time carryforward of up to 20% of unused funds into year 2 (subject to term and approval). Refunds are only available in narrow exceptions and require executive sign-off.

3) Invoice cadence & sample ledger:
- Invoice at prepay: we issue an invoice at the time of prepayment (DocuSign MOA + PO required).
- Monthly statement: we emit a monthly consumption statement and an amortization worksheet for FP&A.

Worked example (simplified):
- Year 1 prepay: $360,000 (committed annual value) at 15% discount (2yr illustrative) -> list-equivalent $423,529
- Consumption profile: baseline months = 1,000k tokens/month; spike months (Q1/Q3) = 3,000k tokens/month (3x peak multiple)
- Wallet drawdown: tokens converted to USD at time of consumption; month with spikes will show higher $ consumption and reduce the wallet accordingly.
- Carryforward option: if Year 1 consumption = 70% of committed spend, up to 20% of the remaining prepaid balance may be applied to Year 2 under the agreed MOA.

I attached a simple amortization invoice example and the detailed waterfall that shows per-month starting balance, consumption, amortized expense, and ending balance. Hope this helps procurement and FP&A. If acceptable, Rafael and I can prep an MOA draft with the 2-year pricing band (15%) and the 20% carryforward clause included.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
